subject.title: Bug: Billing error (402) causes infinite retry death spiral for inline-apiKey providers (no backoff)

question: Should OpenClaw accept provider-scoped persisted cooldown state for inline `models.providers.<id>.apiKey` credentials as the long-term fix for this issue?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible, but the active fix changes compatibility-sensitive auth-provider behavior by making inline keys fail closed during cooldown and by adding a durable provider-level usage namespace.

options.title: Accept provider-scoped inline cooldown
options.body: Proceed with the linked fix path once the PR is clean, reviewed, and the fail-closed cooldown contract is explicitly accepted.

options.title: Request a different compatibility shape
options.body: Ask for a narrower design, migration, or explicit opt-in if persisted fail-closed inline-key cooldown is not acceptable for existing users.

options.title: Document auth profiles only
options.body: Decline provider-level inline cooldown and steer users to auth profiles plus cooldown config, leaving inline keys outside the cooldown system.

recommendation.title: Accept provider-scoped inline cooldown
recommendation.body: Proceed with the linked fix path once the PR is clean, reviewed, and the fail-closed cooldown contract is explicitly accepted.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent auth-profile usage and provider-auth warmup history makes this the strongest routing candidate for the compatibility-sensitive auth decision.
